IMPROVEMENT_TOWN.text: A Hamlet and its upgrades, Village and Town, produce extra Money if brought into your Trade Network.

IMPROVEMENT_VILLAGE.text: A Hamlet and its upgrades, Village and Town, produce extra Money if brought into your Trade Network.

LAW_ORTHODOXY.text: A Disciple can spread your State Religion to other Cities. With the Orthodoxy law, they can also purge other Religions from your Cities.

NATION_MAURYA.text: Maurya, Yuezhi, and Tamilakam share Hinduism as their Pagan Religion.

NATION_TAMIL.text: Maurya, Yuezhi, and Tamilakam share Hinduism as their Pagan Religion.
Coalition Nations, such as Tamilakam, have a different bonus depending on the current Family Supremacy.
In a Coalition Nation, such as Tamilakam, each Character in a Job or Council position will contribute to their Family's Control.
In a Coalition Nation, such as Tamilakam, a Family with higher Control than the leading Family will try to take the throne, making their Family Seat the Capital and their Family Head the Leader.

NATION_YUEZHI.text: Maurya, Yuezhi, and Tamilakam share Hinduism as their Pagan Religion.

PROJECT_LAVISH_LIFESTYLE.text: To gain Victory Points from Opulence, a City requires Estates, and Estates require Luxuries sent to the City.

PROJECT_SUPPRESS_DISSENT_ZOROASTRIANISM.text: A Governor can remove Religious Dissent from their City, such as with the Suppress Zoroastrian Dissent Project.

RESOURCE_BARLEY.text: Boosts Food, which units consume every turn. If built over resources like Wheat or Barley or next to a Granary, also increases Growth, which makes cities produce Settlers or Workers faster. Can be further improved by developing a Farmer.

RESOURCE_CAMEL.text: Provides yields depending on the resource it's built on. If built on Elephants or Camels, will allow the City to build units that require those resources, once the necessary technology is acquired. Extra effective next to a Lumbermill.

RESOURCE_ELEPHANT.text: Provides yields depending on the resource it's built on. If built on Elephants or Camels, will allow the City to build units that require those resources, once the necessary technology is acquired. Extra effective next to a Lumbermill.

RESOURCE_GEM.text: Boosts Iron production, which is needed for many military units. Higher output on Hills. Provides Money instead if built on Silver, Gold, Salt or Gems. Can be developed with a Miner, which increases Training.

RESOURCE_GOLD.text: Boosts Iron production, which is needed for many military units. Higher output on Hills. Provides Money instead if built on Silver, Gold, Salt or Gems. Can be developed with a Miner, which increases Training.

RESOURCE_HORSE.text: Provides Orders if built on Horses, or Food and Growth on other resources.

RESOURCE_SALT.text: Boosts Iron production, which is needed for many military units. Higher output on Hills. Provides Money instead if built on Silver, Gold, Salt or Gems. Can be developed with a Miner, which increases Training.

RESOURCE_SILVER.text: Boosts Iron production, which is needed for many military units. Higher output on Hills. Provides Money instead if built on Silver, Gold, Salt or Gems. Can be developed with a Miner, which increases Training.

RESOURCE_WHEAT.text: Boosts Food, which units consume every turn. If built over resources like Wheat or Barley or next to a Granary, also increases Growth, which makes cities produce Settlers or Workers faster. Can be further improved by developing a Farmer.

SPECIALISTCLASS_FARMER.text: Boosts Food, which units consume every turn. If built over resources like Wheat or Barley or next to a Granary, also increases Growth, which makes cities produce Settlers or Workers faster. Can be further improved by developing a Farmer.

SPECIALISTCLASS_MINER.text: Boosts Iron production, which is needed for many military units. Higher output on Hills. Provides Money instead if built on Silver, Gold, Salt or Gems. Can be developed with a Miner, which increases Training.

SPECIALISTCLASS_PRIEST.text: You can increase Happiness by connecting your Cities with Roads, recruiting Priests, and building Baths. Certain other combinations of Improvements, Specialists, and laws reduce Discontent as well.

SPECIALISTCLASS_STONECUTTER.text: Boosts Stone production, which is needed to construct most buildings and some units. Can be further developed with Stonecutter, which grants more stone and additional Civics.

TECH_LAND_CONSOLIDATION.text: Jungle requires the Land Consolidation Technology to cut down.

TRAIT_CLERGY_CHRISTIAN.text: The Magus, Kohen, Presbyter and Elect Traits mark out Characters as Clergy of their respective Religion.

TRAIT_CLERGY_JEWISH.text: The Magus, Kohen, Presbyter and Elect Traits mark out Characters as Clergy of their respective Religion.

TRAIT_CLERGY_MANICHAEAN.text: The Magus, Kohen, Presbyter and Elect Traits mark out Characters as Clergy of their respective Religion.

TRAIT_CLERGY_ZOROASTRIAN.text: The Magus, Kohen, Presbyter and Elect Traits mark out Characters as Clergy of their respective Religion.

TRAIT_GREEDY.text: Any given Character can have a maximum of three good Traits like Vigilant, and three bad Traits like Greedy.

TRAIT_ORATOR_ARCHETYPE.text: Tribal Mercenary Units can be hired from Tribes by Carthage and by Nations with Orator Leaders.

TRAIT_STRESSED.text: Being Stressed prevents Missions to Influence people! You can Indulge in Revelry to remove stress.

TRAIT_VIGILANT.text: Any given Character can have a maximum of three good Traits like Vigilant, and three bad Traits like Greedy.

TRIBE_BARBARIANS.text: Barbarians are xenophobic Tribes hostile to all Nations. There are no diplomatic consequences for attacking their Units or taking over their land. They have no allies, including other Tribes.

TRIBE_HUNS.text: Huns are a particularly dangerous Tribe. They use the same AI as Player Nations.

TRIBE_RAIDERS.text: Beware of the map edges. Raiders could be lurking beyond!

TRIBE_REBELS.text: Angry Families can rebel against your rule, spawning Rebel Units around their Cities. Your Units from that Family are not as effective when fighting against their own Rebels.
Slums might eventually become profitable Hamlets... but in the meantime they are a recruiting ground for Rebels.

UNIT_CHARIOT.text: Ranged, Mounted, Horse, Chariot, High Vision
Melee, Mounted, Horse, Chariot, Rout, Circle

UNIT_CONSCRIPT.text: Militia and Conscript Units cannot be Promoted, but they are produced with Growth instead of Training. Cities with high Growth output may be able to train them rapidly.

UNIT_HINDUISM_DISCIPLE.text: A Hinduism Disciple cannot spread Hinduism, but can found Theologies and build Improvements such as the Hindu Monastery.
A Hinduism Disciple gives Civics when placed on a Shrine.

UNIT_MILITIA.text: Militia and Conscript Units cannot be Promoted, but they are produced with Growth instead of Training. Cities with high Growth output may be able to train them rapidly.

UNIT_SCOUT.text: Scouts can keep an eye on a large number of Tiles. They can provide valuable intelligence regarding enemy strength and movements.
Cities with high Growth train new Settlers, Workers, and Scouts more rapidly.
Scouts are Hidden while on a Trees Tile in Neutral or Friendly territory.
Scouts, Settlers, and Workers can Harvest Resources for a quick supply of Goods.

Scouts can establish Agent Networks in Foreign Cities. Subsequently, you can assign Characters as Agents to gain visibility of the City and its territory. Agents can also perform Treachery or Insurrection Missions on their Cities.

UNIT_SETTLER.text: Cities with high Growth train new Settlers, Workers, and Scouts more rapidly.
Scouts, Settlers, and Workers can Harvest Resources for a quick supply of Goods.
A Grand Vizier won't be able to build new Settlers and military Units if the necessary national resource stockpiles are too low.

YIELD_HAPPINESS.text: When a City's Happiness meter is filled, its overall Happiness Level goes up, which increases Growth and reduces Maintenance.
You can increase Happiness by connecting your Cities with Roads, recruiting Priests, and building Baths. Certain other combinations of Improvements, Specialists, and laws reduce Discontent as well.
Adopting a State Religion improves that Religion's Opinion of your Nation and also both increases Happiness and enables the recruitment of Disciples in your Cities of that Religion.
Luxuries can be traded to a City to increase Happiness. They can also be traded to other Nations, Tribes, and Families to improve their Opinion of your Nation.

The Cities of Families with a high Opinion of you cost less Maintenance, and their Units fight more effectively.
The Cities of Families with a low Opinion of you cost more Maintenance. Their Units fight less effectively too!

If you don't want to use all of your Orders, you can end your turn by pressing [End + Turn].
Being at War against several opponents can leave your armies overwhelmed, unable to execute enough Orders to fight effectively on every front. Use diplomacy to avoid this fate.
Roads help Units move farther with each Order spent, especially when the Road passes through difficult terrain. They also extend your Trade Network.
Growing your number of Orders should be a priority. The more territory and Units that you control, the more Orders your Nation will need to function and to defend itself.
Ranged Units are efficient in battle, often attacking an enemy without having to spend Orders on movement.
Consider dealing with Events early in your turn. Some Event options require you to spend Orders.
A Forced March permits a Unit to continue moving on the current turn when Fatigued, at the cost of 100 Training and twice as many Orders per additional Move.
Legitimacy is obtained by achieving Ambitions and acquiring better Cognomens (such as the Great). Higher Legitimacy improves Family Opinions and produces more Orders per turn.

Quarries built next to Mountains produce more Stone for each adjacent Mountain Tile. Quarries gain a minor increase when they are built in Arid Terrain.
Most Urban Improvement types require Stone to construct. Expect high demand for Stone as the game matures and you unlock new technologies.
Urban Improvements require extra Stone when built on Hills.
Boosts Stone production, which is needed to construct most buildings and some units. Can be further developed with Stonecutter, which grants more stone and additional Civics.

YIELD_WOOD.text: Your Workers can chop Wood from nearby Trees. The trees will regrow in several years if they aren't completely removed.
If your territory has scant supplies of Wood, consider training military Units that rely on Stone or Iron. Concentrate your limited Wood supply on building Rural Tile Improvements.
Lumbermills built adjacent to Camps gain increased Wood output, as the hunters control predators and forge trails through the forest.
Researching your way to the Lumbermill Improvement takes time. You may need to send Workers to forests and thickets outside your borders, to Chop Wood from Trees and Scrub.
The only Improvement that provides Wood. Extra effective when built on a river.
